guide.text: The sources are Harborlight's FY26 program report and notes from a September 13 board retreat.
Harborlight enrolled 1,148 adult learners in fiscal year 2026, up from 936, and 71 earned a high school equivalency credential.
Operating expenses were $1,420,000, and 287 adults were on the waitlist at year end.
Staff recommend an FY2027 budget of $1,610,000 to add a sixth site at the Eastgate branch library and two site coordinators.
Reserves stand at 3.2 months of operating expenses, below the board's 4-month target, and the board will vote on October 21.

questions.text: 287 adults are waiting an average of nine weeks. Will a sixth site serving 180 more learners a year really cut the waitlist in half?
Enrollment grew by 212, from 936 to 1,148, yet 287 people still wait. Will demand keep outrunning new sites?

brief.goal: Support the sixth site at Eastgate

case: The readers are funders whom board members will meet to talk about the sixth site. They must come away believing that Harborlight's demand has outgrown five sites, that the work gets results, and that a site at the Eastgate branch library is the right next step. The strongest evidence: enrollment grew from 936 to 1,148, 287 adults were still waiting at year end, mostly at Eastgate and Riverside, and 71 learners earned a credential, the most in the organization's history. Funders will ask what it costs and who pays now. The current cost per learner is $1,237, and three funding sources cover a $1,420,000 budget. The ask is $190,000 more a year. That is the gap between the FY2026 operating expenses and the proposed FY2027 budget of $1,610,000, which pays for the Eastgate site and two site coordinators.

P7.text: Present: board chair Lorraine Okafor, treasurer Dev Patel, executive director Marcus Bell, communications director Denise Alvarez, six board members.

P8.text:
The treasurer reported that reserves stand at 3.2 months of operating expenses, below the board's target of 4 months.
The board asked staff to bring a one-page summary of the FY2027 budget request to the October 21 board meeting.
Board members asked for a short deck they can use with funders when they talk about the sixth site.
The board agreed to vote on the FY2027 budget on October 21.

P1.text:
In fiscal year 2026, Harborlight enrolled 1,148 adult learners across five neighborhood sites, up from 936 the year before. Of those learners, 412 were working toward a high school equivalency credential and 389 were English language learners.
Sixty-eight percent of learners who stayed at least 12 weeks gained one or more reading levels on the CASAS assessment. Seventy-one learners earned a high school equivalency credential, the most in the organization's history.

P2.text: A corps of 214 volunteer tutors gave 9,870 tutoring hours. The average tutor stayed 14 months. Harborlight employs 11 full-time staff, including four site coordinators.

P3.text:
Operating expenses for FY2026 were $1,420,000. Program costs were 81 percent of spending. Foundation grants provided $640,000, individual donors gave $388,000, and the city's adult education contract paid $295,000.
The cost per learner was $1,237.

P4.text: At year end, 287 adults were on the waitlist, most of them at the Eastgate and Riverside sites. The average wait was nine weeks.

P5.text:
Staff recommend that the board approve an FY2027 budget of $1,610,000, which adds a sixth site at the Eastgate branch library and two site coordinators. Staff estimate the sixth site would serve 180 more learners a year and cut the waitlist in half.
“I read my granddaughter a bedtime story for the first time this spring,” said a learner at the Riverside site.
